title: Magnetic Skyrmion Interacting with Optical Skyrmion
authors: Lan Bo, Jian Chen, Xichao Zhang, Yan Zhou, Chengwei Qiu, Masahito Mochizuki
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions (MSks) and optical skyrmions (OSks) embody topology in matter and in light, respectively. Here we investigate the interaction between a single MSk and an OSk beam. Three distinct nonlinear dynamical modes are identified: rotation, skipping, and trochoidal motion. By decomposing the optical driving force into gradient, orbital-angular-momentum, and spin-angular-momentum contributions, we clarify their respective roles of radial confinement, azimuthal drift, and precessional modulation. The skipping motion arises from the azimuthal asymmetry of the OSk beam and exhibits spatial selectivity originating from the magnetization-polarization coupling between the MSk and OSk. In three dimensions, the coupling acquires a propagation-dependent phase dominated by the differential Gouy phase, which yields $z$-asymmetric skipping trajectories. These results bridge topological particles and topological fields within a unified framework, offering helicity-selective and phase-programmable routes to optomagnonic control.
summary: This paper investigates the complex interaction between magnetic skyrmions and structured optical beams carrying orbital and spin angular momentum. By decomposing the driving force into distinct components, the authors identify three unique dynamical modes—rotation, skipping, and trochoidal motion. The results demonstrate that this coupling enables precise, phase-programmable control over magnetic topological matter using light.
main_problem: The study investigates how a single Magnetic Skyrmion (MSk) interacts with an Optical Skyrmion (OSk) beam to achieve topology-enabled control over the MSk's dynamics.
main_result: Three distinct nonlinear dynamical modes—rotation, skipping, and trochoidal motion—are identified. The coupling allows for helicity-selective and phase-programmable optomagnonic control.
method: The analysis uses an optomagnetic effective-field picture, decomposing the optical driving force into gradient, OAM, and SAM contributions to model the MSk's response via modified LLG or Thiele equations.
model_or_system: The system involves magnetic skyrmions (topological particle) driven by structured light beams carrying orbital and spin angular momentum (OSk). The dynamics are governed by coupling terms derived from the optical drive field acting on the MSk magnetization.
key_observables: MSk core trajectories, skipping index $\Xi(\phi)$, rotational/skipping velocities $v(\phi)$, and the dependence of skipping azimuth ($\phi_s$) on OSk helicity ($	heta_h$).
important_parameters: Damping constant ($\alpha$), Laguerre-Gaussian mode indices ($l_0$), and the Gouy phase $\zeta(z)$ in 3D propagation.
main_assumptions: The model assumes an externally prescribed optical drive, neglecting magnetization-to-optical feedback. The rigid-particle approximation is used for MSk center dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate LG modes and Poincaré sphere mappings; Fig. 2 shows velocity dependence and trajectories for the three dynamical modes; Fig. 3 details the components of the optical force ($\mathbf{F}_{	ext{grad}}$, $\mathbf{F}_{	ext{OAM}}$, $\mathbf{F}_{	ext{SAM}}$); Fig. 4 visualizes 3D beam structure and $z$-dependent skipping.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical context (MSk/OSk interaction), models the dynamics using force decomposition, identifies three distinct nonlinear modes (rotation, skipping, trochoidal motion) through analytical and numerical simulation, and extends the analysis to 3D propagation effects.
why_interesting: This work bridges topological concepts from condensed matter magnetism (skyrmions) with quantum optics (structured light), providing a framework for controlling magnetic states using tailored optical fields, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems and light-matter interaction studies.
